title: I used four mid-range laptops for a week (demo transcript)
note: Synthetic transcript used for offline testing. The sponsor read starts at the 'this video is sponsored by Kestrel' line.

cues.text: hey everyone welcome back to the channel
today we are finally doing the thing that about four hundred of you have asked for in the comments
we are taking the new mid range laptops and putting them through a full week of real work
not a benchmark run not a synthetic score an actual week of my actual job
so that means video editing in the morning a lot of browser tabs in the afternoon and some light gaming at night
and I want to say up front that the results genuinely surprised me on two of these machines
we have got four laptops on the desk today all of them between eight hundred and twelve hundred dollars
and the plan is simple same workload same settings same week
I have been running these since the start of the month so this is not a first impressions video
before we get into the numbers though let me set up how I tested because I think the method matters here
every machine got a clean install nothing carried over no bloat removed either
whatever the manufacturer ships is what you get because that is what you would actually experience
battery tests were done at two hundred nits with the same playlist running and the same background apps
and the thermal numbers were taken in the same room at the same ambient temperature which was about twenty two degrees
okay so with that out of the way let me quickly talk about who is making today's video possible
this video is sponsored by Kestrel which is a tool I have actually been using since well before they reached out
Kestrel is a password manager and a passkey manager that works across every device you own
and the reason I switched to it is honestly the sharing model
if you have ever tried to share a wifi password or a streaming login with your family you know how bad this usually is
with Kestrel you make a shared vault you drop the credential in and everyone who needs it has it instantly
and if someone leaves you pull their access in one click and the credential rotates automatically
they also do not have access to your vault contents at all everything is encrypted before it leaves your device
they have been independently audited twice now and the reports are public on their site which I appreciate
setup took me about ten minutes including importing everything out of my browser which was frankly a mess
if you want to try it head to kestrel dot com slash channel or use the link in the description
that link gets you three months free on the family plan and it does help the channel out quite a lot
alright thank you Kestrel now let us get back to the laptops
so the first machine is the one I expected the least from and it ended up being my favorite of the group
it is the one with the smaller battery and the slower on paper processor
but the chassis stays cool it never once throttled during an export and the keyboard is genuinely excellent
the display is the weak point it is a sixty hertz panel and the color coverage is not great for editing
but for writing code or writing documents it is completely fine and honestly quite pleasant
the second machine is the opposite story very fast in short bursts and very loud after about ten minutes
if your work is spiky that machine is great if your work is sustained you will hate the fans
I ran the same four minute export on each of them five times across the week and took the average
the fast one won the first run by a wide margin and then lost every subsequent run as it heated up
that is the kind of thing a benchmark chart will never show you which is really the point of this whole video
the third laptop is the one most of you are probably considering because it is the one that gets recommended everywhere
and it is fine it is completely fine it does nothing badly and nothing especially well
the battery lasted about seven and a half hours in my mixed workload which is respectable but not class leading
the fourth one I want to talk about separately because it has a repairability story that is genuinely different
the bottom panel comes off with four captive screws and the battery the storage and the wireless card are all user replaceable
that matters more than a few percent of performance if you plan on keeping the machine for five years
so where does that leave us if you are buying today
if you edit video buy the third one the color accuracy is the thing you cannot fix later
if you write code or write for a living buy the first one the keyboard and the thermals will make you happier every day
if you want to keep it forever buy the fourth one
and if you want the highest peak numbers on a chart buy the second one and accept the noise
let me know down in the comments which of these you would pick and why because I do read all of them
and if there is a machine you want me to add to the next round tell me and I will try to get one in
thanks for watching I will see you in the next one
